script='''#!/usr/bin/env python3
"""Audit frozen u519 archived ABBA/trace claims; no receiver execution."""

summary = qual['summary']

base_r = [x['resident_seconds'] for x in looks if x['route']=='p2w12']
cand_r = [x['resident_seconds'] for x in looks if x['route']=='p3w18']
base_c = [x['complete_lifecycle_seconds'] for x in looks if x['route']=='p2w12']
cand_c = [x['complete_lifecycle_seconds'] for x in looks if x['route']=='p3w18']
assert len(base_r)==len(cand_r)==len(base_c)==len(cand_c)==2
med_b, med_c = statistics.median(base_r), statistics.median(cand_r)
ratios = [c/b for b,c in zip(base_r,cand_r)]
resident_gain = 1-med_c/med_b

assert qual['status']=='performance_gate_rejected'

print(f"busy cores baseline={summary['busy_baseline']:.2f} candidate={summary['busy_candidate']:.2f}")

report='''# u519 historical continuation findings

## Decision

The proposed rejection of the three-owner, 18-worker route (`p3w18`) should stand. Its one-look seven-window screen selected it for a predeclared independent qualifier; the screen was a selector, not proof of adoption. The four-look 13-window ABBA completed with full receiver-work coverage and matching exposed work/message results. The paired resident service medians were 18.613 s (`p2w12`) and 17.889 s (`p3w18`), a 3.92% reduction. The gate required at least 15%, and both paired ratios below 1; the ratios (0.9455, 0.9772) satisfy the latter but not the decisive magnitude gate. Complete-lifecycle median improved 6.69%, within the allowed 5% regression bound. Recomputed average busy-core equivalents rose from 4.12 to 5.78, but utilization alone does not satisfy the speed objective. The independent receipt audit verified hashes/inputs while running, full selected-span union/envelope/gap arithmetic, parity, memory checks and CPU accounting; zero fallback/retry. The performance gate itself was intentionally rejected, so this evidence supports retaining the prior two-owner/default behavior and not adopting the wider route.

## Historical trace and scheduling opportunity

The earlier `c54e24698c69c79805b5aad86205abdd36d2ca7c` trace is a separate, source-bound checkpoint, not the later ABBA candidate. Its matched control and trace outer services were 18.8923 s and 18.8647 s (observer ratio -0.15%); the trace covered five windows, source/input unchanged and exact numeric parity. The observed scheduler starts the first window at 12 workers, then uses two independent owners at 6 workers each. In this capture, job 0 completes at about 5.80 s, jobs 1 and 2 are dispatched back-to-back, and subsequent work is refilled as results arrive (jobs 1/2 complete about 11.64/13.38 s, then jobs 3/4 are submitted). The source enforces an aggregate worker cap, at most two owner processes, one immutable job per owner, bounded IPC/RSS, and public-order commits. This is rolling two-owner concurrency with completion-driven refill, not evidence of 12 continuously busy threads: observed trace establishes chronology but `thread_time_ns` is per-thread and inclusive parent waits are not OS CPU-running evidence. Fine tracking dominates each child slot-score span (about 3.2–3.5 s thread CPU on ~5–6 s wall spans in sampled jobs), while coarse acquisition/selection is around 0.01–0.03 s thread CPU. The actionable narrow scheduling question is whether refilling an owner only after `poll()` completion leaves a material idle gap at realistic full-suite load; if revisited, measure the existing dispatch/IPC/refill spans against actual OS per-thread CPU and leave admission limits intact. Do not reopen wider owner/worker counts on the basis of this earlier checkpoint: later ABBA already tested wider routes and rejected their service gain.

## Recommended next action and prerequisites

First carry this disposition into the active project decision: leave `p3w18` unadopted; keep the separately retained descriptor improvement only if it is present in the eventual current checkout and independently validated. Next, complete the user-visible objective with full manually specified suite CPU forecasts on the actual retained/current source, then benchmark representative bottleneck cases with 12-thread execution and margin measurement. This packet cannot establish current source state, manual-suite inventory, forecast runner entry point/interpreter/dependencies, native binary/fixture identity, RunPod GPU path, or the descriptor change's qualification; the ABBA implementation and private runner were retired/not included. Therefore **do not launch a dependent measurement from this packet**. The engineering owner must first provide the current checkout/revision and dirty-file inventory, native binary/artifacts and fixture hashes, exact manual-case list plus supported forecast/benchmark command and Python/runtime dependencies, CPU capacity denominator, and any GPU toolchain/RunPod transfer path if GPU forecasting remains in scope. Then predeclare outcome-level gates (complete full-suite work, exact parity/input identities, 12-thread CPU margin and complete-lifecycle coverage; GPU forecast accuracy versus CPU reference) and use the repository's supported runner. This continuation did not perform project work, builds, live benchmarks or external research.

## Requirements, choices, assumptions, limits

- Hard from historical user: complete current full-suite CPU estimates; productive use of 12 available hardware threads with credible margin; a fast GPU-assisted future forecast method; preserve received receiver outcome/accuracy; avoid endless measurement/tooling changes. User authorized RunPod spending up to 8 hours/$20 per hour in the historical conversation, but this delegated frozen-packet assignment does not authorize live cloud execution.
- Predeclared ABBA requirements (case-specific): exact same received capture/calendar per route; complete 13-window service; matching exposed work/order/messages; no fallback/retry; 5 GiB common cap; ≥15% median resident-service gain, both paired ratios <1, and no >5% median cold lifecycle regression. Adjustable screen/qualifier choices remain limited to the predeclared routes and winner; do not silently weaken gates.
- Assumptions: the disposition under review is the documented retirement/rejection of p3w18 and retention of the existing two-owner path. The later source is not reconstructed; do not attribute ABBA performance figures to the earlier c54 source or claim those receipts prove today's current source.
- Executable artifact: `check_receipts.py` uses Python 3 standard library only, reads frozen packet JSON, recalculates medians/ratios and checks the rejection/audit invariants. It is a receipt discriminator, not a receiver test. Run: `python3 /tmp/objective-recovery-runs/u519/scratch/check_receipts.py`.
'''
(p/'result.md').write_text(report)
